evidence: The dependency-neutral ObjectStore port now exposes categorized usage, soft/hard/low-disk pressure, preview, and one-time cleanup execution. Accounting separates canonical metadata, durable/derived objects, orphans, indexes, caches, models, configuration, exports, operational state, and an explicit non-overlapping shared-cache authority.

Preview returns only categories, aggregate counts/bytes, and recompute/redownload/repair recovery meaning—never paths or content identities. Cleanup consumes a random one-time bounded token and rechecks immutable document references, active readers, canonical path authority, stable file identity, size, mtime, regular-file type, and single-link status before each destructive step.

Only unreferenced derived-rebuildable canonical objects are automatic mark/sweep candidates. Project-lifetime/export-retained objects, newly referenced objects, held readers, hardlinks, changed same-size cache files, redirected paths, and overlapping shared-cache roots are retained. Audit publication failure denies deletion.

Project hard quota and the local free-space reserve reject new streaming writes with RO-CORE-OBJECT-STORAGE-PRESSURE while verified reads, preview, and cleanup remain available. Partial cleanup uses same-volume staging and restart removes only exclusive operation partials before a fresh preview resumes remaining candidates.

Seven direct maintenance tests cover categorized usage/preview/audit and reference safety; post-preview reference, reader, and same-size cache mutation races; hard quota and low-disk read continuity; interrupted cleanup restart/resume; shared-cache overlap denial; hardlink nonreclamation; and audit-failure byte preservation.

Seven performance-authority tests cover exact baseline/calibration retention, source/sample/latency/throughput threshold laundering, nearest-rank full-sample distributions, unrounded false-green boundaries, explicit nonqualifying calibration reports, all-gate qualification, and stale-report demotion on failure.
The exact complete profile passes 92 data tests and 15 contract tests in addition to the foundation suite and two production performance gates.

The strict portable object-store profile and schema now bind accounting categories, project/shared soft and hard limits, low-disk admission and read continuity, preview/lease behavior, reference and reader rechecks, GC/cache/orphan policies, restart cleanup, shared-cache authority, and content-free audit records. The contract test requires that exact profile.

The architecture guide documents the implemented authority, recovery behavior, security rechecks, CAP-02.S05 shared-cache handoff, and the commit-bound Windows benchmark methodology and budgets. No schema migration is required because usage, references, preview candidates, and recovery state are derived from the current canonical database plus filesystem authority rather than a drift-prone durable counter.

The data profile now includes a versioned three-run Windows baseline and encrypted PDF/report/model throughput plus 2,100-item accounting/GC-pause gate. It complements the existing project-open latency gate and records hardware/OS, fixture/method version, retained samples, absolute budgets, 20% regression thresholds, source hashes, commit, and baseline hash.
No user-interface or approved-reference bytes changed. Shared-cache physical layout remains an explicit later CAP-02.S05 handoff, and no hosted or unrelated capability implementation was introduced.
